prompt: Rank social proof by persuasive strength for an enterprise buyer.

task.prompt: An enterprise healthcare buyer is evaluating you. Rank these forms of social proof from most to least persuasive for them.

items.label: A detailed healthcare case study with measured results
Verified reviews on a B2B review platform
A reference call with a similar healthcare client

task.explanation: Proof is stronger when it is specific, similar to the buyer and verifiable. A conversation with a peer beats anything you write yourself.

prompt: Find the problems in this review request email.

task.prompt: Mark the lines in this email asking a client for a review that should not be sent.

segments.text: Hi Sam, thanks again for working with us on the clinic app.
Would you be willing to share an honest review of your experience on our review profile?
As a thank-you, we'll send a $100 gift card for every 5-star review.
segments.issue: Paying for positive reviews is misleading and usually breaks review platforms' rules.

segments.text: To save time, I've written the review for you; just post it under your name.
segments.issue: Reviews must be the client's own words; ghost-writing is deceptive.

segments.text: It takes about five minutes and here is the direct link.
Either way, thank you for the great collaboration.

prompt: Respond to a negative public review.

task.prompt: A former client posts a 2-star review on a B2B review site saying your team missed deadlines. Part of it is accurate; the delays were also caused by late content from the client.

steps.question: How do you respond publicly?
options: Argue point by point that it was their fault
Ask the platform to delete it
Calmly thank them, acknowledge what went wrong, briefly note what you've changed, and invite a direct conversation
Ignore it
steps.explanation: Prospects read your reply more than the review; a calm, accountable response builds trust.

steps.question: Internally, what should happen next?
options: Blame the delivery team
Post fake positive reviews to bury it
Nothing
Review the project to find what you can improve, such as clearer content deadlines in contracts
steps.explanation: Treat the review as feedback; fix the process that caused it.

prompt: Work out how many reviews you need to lift your rating.

task.prompt: Your profile has 25 reviews averaging 4.6. Assume all new reviews are 5 stars.

fields.label: Total stars from the current reviews
New 5-star reviews needed to reach a 4.8 average

task.explanation: Current total = 25 × 4.6 = 115. Solve (115 + 5n) ÷ (25 + n) = 4.8: 115 + 5n = 120 + 4.8n, so n = 25. Ratings move slowly, so a steady habit of asking happy clients matters more than a one-off push.

task.prompt: A prospect in final evaluation asks to speak with a past client.

steps.question: Which client do you offer?
options: A happy client with a similar project who has agreed to be a reference
Your biggest client, without asking them first
A friend who used to work at a client
Any client who answers the phone
steps.explanation: References should be relevant, willing and prepared.

steps.question: How do you prepare the reference?
options: Give them a script to read
Ask permission, explain who will call and what they care about, and let them speak freely
Offer them a discount to say good things
Don't contact them before the call
steps.explanation: Brief them on context, never on what to say; scripted references sound scripted.

task.prompt: Last year you asked 40 clients for a review after project completion. 14 posted one, averaging 4.7 stars.

fields.label: Clients who did not post a review

task.explanation: 14 ÷ 40 = 35%. 26 did not post. Asking at the right moment (just after a successful launch) and making it easy usually lifts the rate.

prompt: Which piece of social proof is most credible to a careful buyer?

options: A testimonial with no name or company
A statement that you are "trusted by hundreds"
Your own description of your quality
A named, verifiable review from a client in a similar business
mcq.explanation: Specific and verifiable beats vague and self-reported.

prompt: A client asks if they can review you in exchange for a discount on their next project. What should you do?

options: Decline the exchange and ask only for an honest review if they wish to give one
Accept; it is a fair trade
Accept if the review is 5 stars
Offer a larger discount for a longer review
mcq.explanation: Incentivised reviews mislead readers and can breach review platforms' rules.

prompt: When is the best time to ask a client for a review or testimonial?

options: Before the project starts
Soon after a successful milestone, such as launch, when results are fresh
Only after the contract ends a year later
During a dispute, to show goodwill
mcq.explanation: Satisfaction and memory are highest right after a visible success.
